Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  - 3-day history of worsening headache; baseline constant with intermittent worsening; pain 8/10.
  - Location: diffuse, mainly around right eye.
  - Character: dull with intermittent sharp episodes; gradual onset during work.
  - Associated symptoms: photophobia; “shooting lights” at onset; nausea without vomiting; difficulty focusing.
  - No reported fever, rash, head injury, speech difficulty, limb weakness, or loss of vision.
  - Neck pain/stiffness: patient said “Yeah” then “No” (conflict noted).
  - Prior headaches typically responsive to ibuprofen; current episode not responding.
  - Family history of migraines (mother and sister).
  - Uses glasses; no recent eye exam.
  - Occupational screen exposure may exacerbate symptoms.
- Relevant family medical history:
  - Migraines in mother (frequent, seasonal changes trigger) and sister (rare, better controlled).
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):

Management Plan

- Likely migraine discussed given symptom profile and family history.
- Analgesia:
  - Education on correct ibuprofen dosing: up to two tablets three times daily (exact tablet strength not documented).
  - Stronger analgesia discussed: naproxen and/or adding acetaminophen (paracetamol) or codeine.
  - Prescription for stronger analgesia offered; exact medication not documented.
- Self-management:
  - Keep a headache diary to identify triggers.
  - Reduce screen brightness as needed; consider breaks from screen.
  - Consider repeat eye test if eye strain persists.
- Safety-netting:
  - Return or call sooner if worsening headache, vision problems, limb weakness, or feeling generally unwell.
- Follow-up:
  - Review in 1–2 weeks.
  - If headaches become frequent, discuss prophylactic migraine therapy at follow-up.
